title: Retain independent row-offset validation before CSR row-span traversal

masterplan.active_gate: Gate 1 — Renovation, owner-directed Genesis and general computer assistance

scope: Audit TypedRelationBlock.__post_init__ for a removable duplicate validation traversal across row_offsets and the later row-structured column spans. Fuse or delete work only if direct-constructor error precedence, exact-int refusal, start/shape/monotonicity refusal, range-before-common-count precedence, strictly increasing per-row columns, tuple reuse and all bounded limits remain identical.

audit.finding: The apparent second use of row_offsets is not redundant validation. The first complete offsets pass establishes exact-int admission and records monotonicity before any structural row-span access. After length/start/monotonicity acceptance and scalar admission, the matched-count path must consume the same boundaries again to delimit each CSR row while validating per-row column range and strict ordering.
audit.error_precedence: A fused row-by-row offset/column traversal would allow an earlier column error, start-boundary refusal or monotonicity refusal to fire before a later non-integer row offset. The current contract instead fully scans row-offset element types first. For example row_offsets=(1, 0, 'bad') must report 'block.row_offsets must contain integers' even though the sequence also violates start-at-zero and monotonicity. The count-mismatch fallback separately preserves column type then range refusal before common-entry-count refusal.
audit.boundedness: row_offsets is already bounded by MAX_BLOCK_AXIS_LABELS + 1 and canonical tuples are reused. The first pass allocates no per-row state beyond one previous_offset scalar and one boolean. The second use is the actual CSR row-span traversal required to validate column ordering; removing it would require either a parallel trusted constructor, a new row classifier, deferred errors or duplicated structural logic.
audit.gardener_conclusion: Retain the independent row-offset validation boundary and the subsequent row-span traversal. Do not introduce a trusted-constructor bypass, validation flag, second block family or alternate CSR admission path merely to eliminate one bounded pass. Pin the error-precedence counterexample in the existing validation-fusion test owner.

test_change.purpose: Pin that a later non-integer row offset outranks earlier start-boundary and monotonicity violations, which prevents unsafe fusion with row-local column validation.
test_change.history_note: The first contents edit accidentally omitted the pre-existing tail of the test file; the immediate follow-up commit restored it verbatim. The net GPU-92..GPU-93 test diff is only the six-line focused regression contract, and the intermediate commit remains in history rather than being rewritten.

semantic_invariants.scalar_precedence: Persisted scalar admission remains before CSR structural validation.
semantic_invariants.offset_types: All row_offsets must be exact integers before boundary, monotonicity or row-span semantics are accepted.
semantic_invariants.offset_shape: row_offsets must contain exactly one boundary per row plus the terminal boundary and must start at zero.
semantic_invariants.offset_monotonicity: Monotonicity remains a distinct refusal after exact-int and shape/start admission.
semantic_invariants.column_precedence: Column exact-int refusal remains before out-of-range refusal; out-of-range refusal remains before common-entry-count refusal; strict per-row ordering remains after common-count consistency.
semantic_invariants.tuple_reuse: Canonical tuple inputs remain reusable without an extra tuple copy.
semantic_invariants.source_of_truth: KnowledgeForest/Fourfold remain authoritative; TypedRelationBlock remains a regenerable internal computational view.
semantic_invariants.public_api: No public API, wire schema, benchmark schema, authority or promotion contract changes.

result.summary: GPU-93 establishes that the first bounded row-offset pass owns exact-int/error-precedence admission while the later pass is actual row-span CSR validation, not duplicate work. The existing boundary is retained and a focused regression test pins the mixed-invalid counterexample without changing production code.
